decisions.title: ADR 0001: Use Codex app-server authentication for model work
decisions.body:
# ADR 0001: Use Codex app-server authentication for model work

## Status

Accepted.

## Context

The pipeline needs an OpenAI model while avoiding direct handling of API keys or
private Codex credential caches. The requested model is `gpt-5.6-luna` with
reasoning effort `max`. The existing scripts used local OpenAI-compatible HTTP
and an OpenRouter scorer.

## Decision

Use the official `openai-codex` Python SDK to launch an ephemeral, read-only
Codex app-server turn. Let Codex own ChatGPT OAuth. The shared provider seam
records requested model, actual model, reasoning effort, run ID, prompt/output
hashes, provider, and fallback reason. Docker workers call a narrow host-side
gateway instead of receiving OAuth state.

## Consequences

- The exact requested model and effort are explicit in code and environment.
- The pipeline does not read `~/.codex/auth` or make a direct API call with an
  extracted OAuth token.
- A local OpenAI-compatible server remains an explicit fallback and is never
  silently presented as Codex.
- The gateway token is an operator-managed secret and must not enter logs or
  manifests.

## Alternatives considered

Direct API keys were rejected because credential lifecycle and scope would move
into this repository. GPT Actions were rejected because their OAuth flow
authenticates users to third-party action APIs rather than providing local
Python access to an OpenAI model.

decisions.title: ADR 0002: Support host and Docker Airflow through one provider seam
decisions.body:
# ADR 0002: Support host and Docker Airflow through one provider seam

## Status

Accepted.

## Context

Standalone scripts run naturally on the host, while the existing production
workflow runs in Airflow containers. OAuth state should not be copied into each
worker, and the two modes should not develop different prompt or metadata
behavior.

## Decision

Use `CODEX_RUNTIME=host` for direct SDK execution and
`CODEX_RUNTIME=gateway` for Docker. The host gateway accepts only bearer-
authenticated, bounded JSON generation requests and delegates to the same
Codex provider and fallback policy. Airflow pools call the `codex` pool.

## Consequences

Provider selection is configuration, not a fork of every script. Container
workers can use the same exact model, prompt policy, privacy gate, research
mode, and audit metadata. The gateway is an additional process to supervise and
its host token must be provisioned before Docker runs.

## Alternatives considered

Host-only execution was simpler but did not support the existing Compose
deployment. Docker-only login was rejected because interactive OAuth lifecycle
inside workers is fragile and unnecessarily duplicates account state.

decisions.title: ADR 0003: Redact and gate Takeout content before model calls
decisions.body:
# ADR 0003: Redact and gate Takeout content before model calls

## Status

Accepted.

## Context

Google Takeout records can contain identifiers, credentials, and sensitive
health, legal, financial, or employment context. Raw records must remain in
ignored local storage and should not be sent to a model by accident.

## Decision

Manual Takeout acquisition remains outside the pipeline. `takeout_intake.py`
copies into ignored `inbox/` only when explicitly applied and writes a checksum
manifest. The privacy filter redacts common identifiers. Secrets, government
IDs, and high-risk sensitive contexts block model calls by default. An override
must include both an explicit enable flag and a reason, is recorded as a safe
metadata field, and still routes the resulting article to editorial review.

## Consequences

The source tree is never deleted or modified by intake. Model prompts and
research inputs receive sanitized content. Some legitimate technical examples
may require an operator-reviewed override; that trade-off is visible in the
ledger rather than hidden in a prompt.

## Alternatives considered

Sending raw records was rejected for privacy reasons. Blocking every record
with an identifier was rejected because it would discard ordinary technical
material unnecessarily.

decisions.title: ADR 0004: Capture bounded evidence before rewriting
decisions.body:
# ADR 0004: Capture bounded evidence before rewriting

## Status

Accepted.

## Context

Conversation-derived material often contains uncertain or time-sensitive claims.
Rewriting can improve prose while accidentally making unsupported claims sound
authoritative. The project requires recorded sources and review for uncertainty.

## Decision

Use Codex web search as the primary research adapter with a strict source JSON
schema, URL validation, citation metadata, and a bounded source count. If the
Codex research call is unavailable, use the deterministic HTTP adapter as a
fallback and record the failure. Search snippets are never treated as facts.

## Consequences

Research packets become inspectable inputs to rewriting. Official and primary
sources are preferred, but source presence does not remove editorial review for
medical, legal, financial, privacy, regulatory, or time-sensitive claims.

## Alternatives considered

HTTP-only research was predictable but weaker as the primary source-finding
path. Codex-only research had no deterministic availability fallback.

decisions.title: ADR 0005: Keep taxonomy and publication decisions deterministic
decisions.body:
# ADR 0005: Keep taxonomy and publication decisions deterministic

## Status

Accepted.

## Context

The model can suggest a topic or article angle, but a model-created folder or
tag would violate the controlled taxonomy. Publication also needs a reversible,
auditable boundary.

## Decision

`taxonomy.py` remains the only category authority. The article surgeon may
recommend a split but does not control category folders. Every published file
must have exactly one allowlisted Category and exactly one matching Tags value,
with the category slug as its parent. Strict validation runs before atomic
publication. High-confidence ordinary rewrites may auto-publish; privacy,
uncertainty, time-sensitive/regulatory, ambiguous, and explicitly exempt
content routes to review.

## Consequences

The model has useful autonomy over prose and prioritization without authority to
expand the publication taxonomy or bypass safety gates. Migration manifests,
score records, rewrite backups, research packets, and disposition ledgers make
the path inspectable and provide override points.

## Alternatives considered

Fully automatic publication was rejected because a polished unsupported claim
is more dangerous than a rough draft. Manual approval for every ordinary
article was rejected because it would prevent useful bounded autonomy.
